slides.title: Three authors, one trail
slides.text: Your footprint is written by three authors: you, in your own posts; other people, in posts about you; and services, collecting scores, locations and likes.

slides.title: Who wrote this clue?
slides.text: Pim found three clues in one trail. Each clue has a different author.
steps: you share your race photo: you
a friend tags you in theirs: a friend
a game saves your top score: a service

slides.title: Delete is not erase
slides.text: Deleting a post is asking nicely for it to go. Copies, screenshots and shares can keep it alive long after your own copy is gone.

slides.title: Future readers
slides.text: That drawing you posted for feedback stays in your trail. Years later, teammates, schools and employers may read old posts as part of who you are.
slides.alt: A second online dilemma: posting your work brings feedback, and can also show more than you meant.

slides.title: Ask before you post
slides.text: Public gets you seen and found; private keeps you safe. Before you post, ask the Cyber Defender question: what could someone do with this?
slides.alt: An online dilemma in Pro: make it public and be found, or keep it private and stay safe — a real tradeoff.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather and choose the Online topic: play Online: share or keep. For one dilemma, say how a future audience might read that post.
